set_aside.subject: scope of conditional repeatability promises
set_aside.text: Every promise in these documents that a function repeats itself — equal outputs on equal inputs, a repaired slot staying repaired, a verdict that holds — is a promise about code that obtains neither.
set_aside.question: Which exact State 0 obligations are weakened by this condition: only the three listed examples, or every obligation from which repeatability could be inferred, and how is that set identified?
options: Only the three listed promises are conditional
The examples are illustrative and every repeatability-dependent obligation is conditional
A named exhaustive list of conditional obligations is required
set_aside.default_guess: Treat the three listed promises as exhaustive because later implementers cannot reliably infer an open-ended set.

witness.initial: An implementation has been admitted and activated after passing a captured regression case.
events: The owner runs the same flow again with the same function input.
The function produces a different but schema-valid result because it obtained an undeclared source of chance.
An agent inspects the run and the prior admission.
outcomes: The differing result is allowed only with respect to the three named promises; all other repeatability-dependent requirements still apply.
Every requirement that an implementer regards as implying repeatability is suspended, including requirements not named in the change.
witness.observer: The owner and the agent interpreting whether the run violated a product promise

set_aside.subject: meaning and authority for the no-time-or-chance condition
set_aside.question: What exactly counts as obtaining time or chance, including indirect library calls, interpreter hash randomization, process identifiers, scheduling, environment state, or deterministic pseudorandomness seeded from an input; and who or what establishes this fact when the kernel explicitly does not detect alternate access?
options: Only explicit reads from clock or randomness APIs count
Any dependency on execution-state information not present in declared inputs counts
The condition is only a documentation caveat and is never established or stored
set_aside.default_guess: Treat any dependency on information outside declared inputs as obtaining time or chance, but store no classification because the kernel cannot establish it.

witness.initial: A function uses Python hash iteration order, which can vary with the interpreter's per-process seed, but calls no clock or randomness API.
events: The agent submits the implementation and it passes its corpus.
The same declared input is executed in another sandbox process.
A later agent asks whether equal-output and repaired-slot promises apply.
outcomes: The function obtained chance indirectly through the interpreter seed, so the repeatability promises do not apply.
The function obtained neither time nor chance because its code called no such source, so the repeatability promises do apply.
witness.observer: The later agent and owner evaluating the differing output

set_aside.subject: equality used by the repeatability promise
set_aside.question: What equality relation defines equal function inputs and outputs, especially for structured values and files: canonical typed-value equality, serialized-byte equality, stored digest equality, or file-content equality independent of spool identity and metadata?
options: Canonical equality of typed values and file contents
Equality of the kernel's stored digests
Identity of the stored value or spool object
set_aside.default_guess: Use canonical typed-value equality and exact file-content equality, ignoring storage identity.

witness.initial: A function receives a structured value whose object fields can be serialized in more than one order.
events: The function is run twice with logically identical values encoded with different field order.
It emits logically identical structured outputs with different serialization order.
The kernel records output digests and returns the results.
outcomes: The inputs and outputs are equal as typed values, so the repeatability promise is satisfied.
The byte encodings or digests differ, so the repeatability promise is violated.
witness.observer: The owner or agent comparing the two runs

set_aside.subject: lifetime of an admission verdict
set_aside.question: Across which changes must an admission verdict continue to hold: only while the exact trial corpus and implementation are unchanged, or also after cases are added to the contract version's corpus; and what happens to an active implementation when a new case would fail?
options: The verdict remains a historical verdict over its original corpus snapshot and activation continues
Adding a case invalidates the verdict and deactivates or blocks the implementation until readmission
The verdict is automatically re-evaluated against the enlarged corpus
set_aside.default_guess: Treat the verdict as historical over its original corpus snapshot; require a new admission before it can be used for rollback against the enlarged corpus, without silently changing the current activation.

witness.initial: Implementation I is admitted and active for contract version C over corpus containing case A.
events: An agent adds case B to C's corpus.
I would fail B although it obtains neither time nor chance.
The owner starts a flow that uses C.
outcomes: I remains active because its recorded verdict still holds over the corpus on which it was made, so the run starts.
I's verdict no longer holds over the current corpus, so I is no longer usable until admission is run again.

set_aside.subject: repeatability versus sandbox resource variability
set_aside.question: Does the conditional repeatability promise cover only returned values, or also sandbox failures such as timeouts and memory/process-limit failures whose occurrence can vary with host load even when the code obtains neither time nor chance; if it covers them, what execution-environment facts must be fixed or treated as inputs?
options: The promise covers outputs only and permits variable resource failures
The promise covers all execution verdicts, requiring a reproducible sandbox environment
Resource bounds are part of the effective input even though they are not function ports
set_aside.default_guess: Limit deterministic repeatability to successful returned values and do not promise identical timeout or resource-failure outcomes.

witness.initial: A deterministic repaired implementation passes its captured regression case while executing close to its declared time bound.
events: The kernel admits and activates it on a lightly loaded host.
The same declared input is run later while the host is contended.
The sandbox either finishes just before the bound or times out.
outcomes: The repaired-slot promise includes execution success, so the later timeout violates the promise and the implementation must prevent environmental variation.
The promise concerns output determinism only; a later resource failure is allowed despite the same input and no time or chance access.
witness.observer: The owner seeing either a successful run or a failed node
